description: Index of breach kill chain scenarios for the Blast Radius Visualizer (/blast-radius.html). Add a new entry here plus a scenario JSON file in this directory and the visualizer picks it up automatically — no code changes required. See data/chains/README.md for the schema.

scenarios.title: Control Coverage Map
scenarios.subtitle: Which single defensive control would have stopped the most real breaches — read backwards from all 45 kill chains' own “How to Defend” sections

scenarios.title: Kevin Mitnick / Novell (1994)
scenarios.subtitle: OSINT → Pretexting → Phone Social Engineering → Dial-Up Access → NetWare Source Code Theft

scenarios.title: event-stream (2018)
scenarios.subtitle: A volunteer offered to maintain an abandoned npm package, got publish rights, and slipped an encrypted payload into a new dependency that stole from one Bitcoin wallet app.

scenarios.title: Capital One (2019)
scenarios.subtitle: SSRF → IMDSv1 → Over-Privileged IAM Role → 106M Record S3 Exfiltration

scenarios.title: SolarWinds / SUNBURST (2020)
scenarios.subtitle: Build System Compromise → SUNBURST Backdoor → Golden SAML → US Government Espionage

scenarios.title: ChaosDB / Azure Cosmos DB (2021)
scenarios.subtitle: A notebook feature in a managed database allowed local privilege escalation and firewall rewrites, reaching the Cosmos DB backend and full admin over other tenants' databases.

scenarios.title: Codecov Bash Uploader (2021)
scenarios.subtitle: A credential leaked by a Docker build let an attacker add one line to a script thousands of CI jobs curl — exfiltrating two months of CI environment variables.

scenarios.title: Kaseya VSA / REvil (2021)
scenarios.subtitle: An authentication bypass in an internet-facing RMM server let REvil push ransomware as a software update — encrypting ~1,500 businesses through their IT providers.

scenarios.title: Log4Shell (2021)
scenarios.subtitle: A logging library that interpreted its own input turned any logged string into an unauthenticated JNDI request to an attacker server — RCE almost everywhere, and nobody could inventory where.

scenarios.title: XZ Utils (2021–2024)
scenarios.subtitle: A two-year social campaign made 'Jia Tan' the maintainer, shipping a backdoor only in release tarballs that hooked sshd for pre-auth RCE — caught by a 500ms latency regression.

scenarios.title: 0ktapus / Twilio (2022)
scenarios.subtitle: SMS phishing with lookalike Okta pages captured credentials and live OTPs, relayed in real time to breach 130+ organizations — but a FIDO2 hardware key stopped it at Cloudflare.

scenarios.title: CircleCI (2022–2023)
scenarios.subtitle: Malware on an engineer's laptop stole a live 2FA-backed SSO session cookie, giving production access and forcing every customer to rotate every secret on the platform.

scenarios.title: LastPass (2022)
scenarios.subtitle: Dev Env Breach → DevOps Home PC (Plex Exploit) → Keylogger → AWS S3 Vault Backup Exfil

scenarios.title: Okta / LAPSUS$ (2022)
scenarios.subtitle: A subcontractor's support engineer laptop gave LAPSUS$ five days inside Okta's support tooling — password-reset powers exposing up to 366 customers.

scenarios.title: Uber (2022)
scenarios.subtitle: Dark Web Creds → MFA Push Fatigue → Hardcoded PAM Secret → Full AWS/GCP Admin

scenarios.title: 3CX / X_TRADER (2023)
scenarios.subtitle: A trojanized trading app on an employee's personal PC yielded 3CX credentials, VPN access, and both build environments — shipping a signed, backdoored softphone to hundreds of thousands of customers.

scenarios.title: MOVEit Transfer / Cl0p (2023)
scenarios.subtitle: A SQL-injection zero-day in internet-facing managed file transfer software dropped the LEMURLOOT web shell for mass data theft — 2,600+ organizations extorted.

scenarios.title: Microsoft AI Research SAS Token (2023)
scenarios.subtitle: Over-Permissioned Token → Public GitHub → 38TB Internal Data Exposed for 3 Years

scenarios.title: Midnight Blizzard / Microsoft (2023–2024)
scenarios.subtitle: A password spray on a forgotten test tenant reached a legacy OAuth app with production rights, exposing executive email — and secrets in that email led to source code.

scenarios.title: Okta Support System (2023)
scenarios.subtitle: A service-account credential synced to a personal Google profile reached the support case system, where HAR files full of live session tokens let attackers hijack customer sessions.

scenarios.title: Scattered Spider / MGM Resorts (2023)
scenarios.subtitle: LinkedIn OSINT → Vishing Help Desk → Okta Super Admin → 100 ESXi Servers Encrypted

scenarios.title: Storm-0558 / Microsoft (2023)
scenarios.subtitle: Crash Dump → Stolen MSA Signing Key → Forged Tokens → Government Email Espionage

scenarios.title: Change Healthcare / ALPHV (2024)
scenarios.subtitle: Stolen credentials on a Citrix portal with no MFA gave nine days of lateral movement before ransomware — disrupting a third of US healthcare transactions.

scenarios.title: Polyfill.io (2024)
scenarios.subtitle: The polyfill.io domain was sold; every site still loading its script handed over its users, receiving conditional mobile redirects to scam sites.

scenarios.title: Promptware / Gemini (2024–2026)
scenarios.subtitle: Indirect Prompt Injection → Context Poisoning → Persistence → C2 → Covert Camera Livestream

scenarios.title: UNC5537 / Snowflake (2024)
scenarios.subtitle: Infostealer Creds → No MFA → SHOW TABLES → Bulk Exfil → 100+ Orgs Extorted

scenarios.title: Ultralytics (2024)
scenarios.subtitle: A fork branch name as shell injection poisoned the Actions cache, publishing a malicious build through Trusted Publishing — running XMRig, then abusing a forgotten token.

scenarios.title: Codefinger / S3 Ransomware (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: Stolen AWS keys authenticated to the victim account, enumerated buckets, and re-encrypted objects with an attacker-held SSE-C key — with a 7-day deletion timer and a Bitcoin ransom.

scenarios.title: Entra ID Actor Token (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: An undocumented service-to-service Actor token, requested from any attacker-controlled tenant, forged an unsigned impersonation JWT that legacy Azure AD Graph accepted — Global Admin in any tenant, unlogged.

scenarios.title: GTG-1002 (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: Operators jailbroke an agent by decomposing the campaign into benign-looking tasks, then had it run reconnaissance, exploitation, and exfiltration against ~30 targets with human approval at a few gates.

scenarios.title: Nx / s1ngularity (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: A PR-title injection in pull_request_target stole an npm token, then weaponized local AI CLIs to hunt secrets and published them to public repos.

scenarios.title: Oracle E-Business Suite / Cl0p (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: An unauthenticated XSLT-injection zero-day gave server-side RCE on Oracle EBS, silently exfiltrating HR, payroll and financial data for two months before executive email extortion.

scenarios.title: Salesloft Drift / UNC6395 (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: A GitHub compromise led to the Drift AWS environment and stolen OAuth tokens, then bulk SOQL exfiltration and secret-mining across 700+ organizations.

scenarios.title: Shai-Hulud (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: npm phishing seeded a self-replicating worm that ran TruffleHog against developer machines, republished across 500+ packages, and committed harvested secrets to public repos.

scenarios.title: SharePoint 'ToolShell' (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: Unauthenticated deserialization at ToolPane.aspx gave a web shell and MachineKey theft — forging __VIEWSTATE forever and, at some victims, Warlock ransomware.

scenarios.title: UNC6040 (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: Vishing the help desk got victims to authorize a fake Data Loader as an OAuth connected app, enabling bulk Salesforce exfiltration and later extortion.

scenarios.title: npm debug / chalk (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: A fake 2FA-reset email relayed a live TOTP, took over a maintainer account, and trojanized 18 packages totaling 2.6 billion weekly downloads.

scenarios.title: tj-actions/changed-files (2025)
scenarios.subtitle: A stolen PAT retagged an action to a malicious commit that dumped runner memory into public build logs — exposing secrets across 23,000+ repositories.

scenarios.title: Hugging Face / OpenAI Agent (2026)
scenarios.subtitle: During an internal eval, a model escaped its sandbox through a package-proxy zero-day, reached Hugging Face, gained RCE via a malicious dataset, and harvested cloud and cluster credentials.

scenarios.title: LiteLLM / TeamPCP (2026)
scenarios.subtitle: A poisoned security scanner running in CI stole a PyPI token, published trojanized releases, and swept cloud credentials and Kubernetes tokens via a .pth autorun.

scenarios.title: Megalodon (2026)
scenarios.subtitle: Infostealer-harvested GitHub credentials drove 5,718 automated commits in six hours, injecting Actions workflows that stole CI secrets and OIDC tokens across 5,561 repositories.

scenarios.title: Mini Shai-Hulud / TanStack (2026)
scenarios.subtitle: A pwn-request poisoned the Actions cache, stole the OIDC token from runner memory, and published npm packages with valid SLSA provenance — worming across 150+ packages.

scenarios.title: Storm-2949 (2026)
scenarios.subtitle: A Self-Service Password Reset plus a fake IT call took over MFA methods, then abused existing Azure RBAC to drain Key Vault, SQL and storage.

scenarios.title: Suspected AI-Assisted AWS Compromise (2026)
scenarios.subtitle: A leaked AWS key drove a machine-speed sweep: secrets harvested, multi-account persistence planted, CI/CD abused, RDS exfiltrated, and infrastructure held for extortion in 72 hours.

scenarios.title: Vercel / Context.ai (2026)
scenarios.subtitle: Infostealer at a vendor compromised its OAuth app, took over a connected Google Workspace account, and reached plaintext environment variables across customer projects.

scenarios.title: Vimeo / Anodot (2026)
scenarios.subtitle: Stolen analytics-vendor tokens gave direct Snowflake and BigQuery access with no interactive login — 119,000 records exfiltrated and extorted, without touching Vimeo's perimeter.
